text: Griha pravesh, the first entry into a new home, is placed by the Vastu chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani in daylight only. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 13 of either paksha, leaving out the rikta tithis 4, 9 and 14, the 8th, Amavasya and the 1st. The nakshatras are the fixed and soft groups the text names for settling: Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are the allowed weekdays. A pandit may add the Lagna of the hour; this finder scores the panchang rules only.

Buying a vehicle follows the Vahana chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani, in daylight. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, avoiding the rikta tithis 4, 9 and 14 together with the 8th and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the same fixed and soft group used for griha pravesh (Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada, Revati), because a vehicle is read as something to be kept and used steadily. Sunday joins Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday as an allowed weekday. The finder scores these alongside the personal Chandra bala and Tara bala rules.

Opening a business or shop follows the Vyapara verses of the Muhurta Chintamani and the Muhurta Martanda, in daylight. The table allows tithis 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 of either paksha and Purnima, avoiding 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14 and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the fixed and soft group: Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. The window's choghadiya should be Shubh, Labh or Amrit.

Joining a job or attending an interview follows the Seva (service) verses of the Muhurta Chintamani, in daylight. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, avoiding 4, 8, 9, 14 and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the fixed and soft group (Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Revati) with Uttara Bhadrapada left out, as the text prefers for entering another's service. Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. When the date is fixed by the employer, the finder still shows the best hour inside it.

Setting out on a journey follows the Yatra chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani, and night windows are allowed because journeys begin at any hour. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 of either paksha, avoiding the rikta tithis, the 8th, the 12th, Purnima, Amavasya and the 1st. The nakshatras are the nine moving and soft stars the text names for travel: Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Anuradha, Shravana, Dhanishta and Revati. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. Disha Shool, the direction to avoid on each weekday, is shown separately on the Travel today card.

The naming ceremony follows the Samskara chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani, in daylight. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, avoiding the rikta tithis 4, 9 and 14, the 8th, the 6th and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the fixed and soft group: Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. The starting syllable of the name itself comes from the Naamkaran helper.

Mundan, the first haircut (Chudakarana), follows the Samskara chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani, in daylight. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 of either paksha, avoiding the rikta tithis, the 8th, the 12th, Purnima, Amavasya and the 1st. The nakshatras the text names for cutting hair are Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Jyeshtha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha and Revati. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. Families often also follow their own custom about the child's age and month, which the finder does not judge.

Engagement or roka (vagdana, the giving of word) follows the Vivaha chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani and is scored for two profiles, with night windows allowed. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, avoiding 4, 6, 8, 9, 14 and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the eleven marriage stars: Rohini, Mrigashira, Magha, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Mula, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. Chandra bala and Tara bala are checked for both people.

Basic marriage windows follow the Vivaha chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani and the Dharmasindhu, scored for two profiles, day or night. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 13 of either paksha, avoiding the rikta tithis, the 8th, the 6th, Purnima, Amavasya and the 1st. The nakshatras are the eleven marriage stars: Rohini, Mrigashira, Magha, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Mula, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. This is the basic panchang layer only; the Lagna, the Sun's sign, Jupiter and Venus visibility and the family's regional rules are left to a pandit.

Registering or buying property follows the Bhumi kraya (buying land) verses of the Vastu chapter, in daylight. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, avoiding 4, 6, 8, 9, 14 and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the fixed and soft group: Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati, the fixed stars being preferred for anything meant to last. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. Office hours decide the usable part of the window.

A new venture or launch, from a company to a product or a website, uses the same Vyapara table as a business start, in daylight. The table allows tithis 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 of either paksha and Purnima, avoiding 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14 and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the fixed and soft group: Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. A launch set for a fixed day can still pick its best hour here.

Beginning study, a course or a child's first lessons (Vidyarambha) follows the Samskara chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani, in daylight. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 11 and 12 of either paksha, avoiding the rikta tithis, the 7th, 8th, 13th, Purnima, Amavasya and the 1st. The nakshatras the text names for learning are Ashwini, Mrigashira, Ardra, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha and Revati, Ardra being included for its link with Mercury's sharpness. Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed.

A planned, non-emergency medical procedure follows the Aushadha (medicine) and Shastra-karma (surgery) verses of the Muhurta Chintamani, in daylight. The table allows tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 of either paksha, avoiding the rikta tithis, the 8th, the 12th, Purnima, Amavasya and the 1st. The nakshatras are Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. This is a timing custom only: it never replaces the doctor's schedule, and anything urgent should not wait for a window.

Beginning a vow or a series of fasts (vrata-arambha) follows the Dharmasindhu and the Muhurta Chintamani, in daylight. The table allows tithis 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, avoiding 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14 and Amavasya. The nakshatras are the fixed and soft group: Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are allowed. A vrat tied to a fixed tithi, such as Ekadashi, keeps its own date; this finder is for vows that may start on any good day.

The tithi rule checks the lunar day running for most of the window against the activity's allowed list. Every table leaves out the rikta tithis (4th, 9th and 14th) and Amavasya, and most leave out the 8th; the rest varies by activity. Because a tithi can change in the middle of a day, the rule uses the tithi that covers the larger part of the window and shows when it ends.

The nakshatra rule checks the Moon's nakshatra running for most of the window against the activity's allowed list. The classical tables group the 27 stars as fixed, soft, moving, sharp, mixed and so on and match each activity to the groups that suit it; fixed and soft stars for settling, moving stars for travel. The rule uses the nakshatra covering the larger part of the window and shows when it ends.

The vara rule checks the weekday against the activity's allowed list. The Vedic day runs from sunrise to sunrise, so a night window after midnight still belongs to the weekday that began at the previous sunrise. Tuesday and Saturday are left out of every table in this app; Sunday is allowed for some activities, such as a business start, and not for others, such as travel or a marriage.

The Chandra bala rule asks where the transit Moon stands counted from the natal Moon of each profile chosen for the search. The 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th and 11th signs are favourable; the others, and especially the 8th (Chandrashtama), are not. For two-profile activities such as marriage and engagement both Moons must pass. It is the same rule the Today screen uses for the daily note, applied to the day of the window.

The Tara bala rule counts the day's nakshatra from each profile's birth nakshatra and divides by nine. Sampat (2), Kshema (4), Sadhaka (6), Mitra (8) and Param Mitra (9) are favourable taras; Janma (1), Vipat (3), Pratyari (5) and Vadha (7) are not. Every profile in the search must land on a favourable tara for the rule to count as met, and the row names the tara for each.

The Rahu Kaal rule is met when the window does not touch the day's Rahu Kaal, the eighth of the daytime assigned to the weekday. The finder removes Rahu Kaal from every candidate before scoring, so the rule is always met for a listed window and appears in the count so that it reads as one of ten; the row notes when a window was shortened by this clipping and shows the Rahu Kaal times.

The Bhadra rule is met when the window does not overlap a Vishti karana whose residence is earth. Bhadra is the Vishti half-tithi, and the Muhurta Chintamani places it in heaven, on earth or in the underworld by the Moon's sign; only the earth residence is held to matter for beginnings. Windows overlapping an earth Bhadra are kept in the list with this rule failed, so the ranking stays explainable.

The Panchak rule is met when the window does not overlap Panchak, the roughly five-day stretch while the Moon moves from the third pada of Dhanishta to the end of Revati. The tradition sets Panchak aside for five kinds of beginnings, among them building, travel southward and gathering fuel. Windows inside Panchak are shown with this rule failed rather than hidden, and the Travel today card repeats the flag.

The Abhijit rule is a bonus: it is met when the window overlaps the Abhijit muhurta, the 48 minutes centred on local noon that the tradition calls good on every weekday. Abhijit never makes a window by itself; it adds one rule to a window that already exists and breaks ties between windows that meet the same number of rules. The row shows the Abhijit times of the day.

The choghadiya rule is met when every choghadiya segment inside the window is Shubh, Labh or Amrit. Windows are built from choghadiya segments, so a window that spans two segments has to pass on both; Chal counts as neutral and fails the rule, and Rog, Kaal and Udveg fail it too. The row lists the segment names covered by the window in time order.

Windows are ranked by the number of rules met out of ten, highest first; among equals, a window with the Abhijit bonus comes first, then the earlier start, then the longer window. Scores are counts of rules, never probabilities, and the same order is used for the partial matches. A window meeting fewer than four rules is listed only under Best partial matches, and windows overlapping Bhadra or Panchak are kept with those rules shown as failed, so every position in the list can be traced to its rows.
